transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been feeling really restless. Like if I’m supposed to sit still—staff meetings, church briefings, that kind of thing—it feels like there’s a motor running under my skin. I end up shifting around, standing up, or finding some reason to move.
Did this restless feeling start after you began taking a medication or after the dose of one was changed?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed it lining up with any medication change.
Did you have this kind of hard-to-sit-still restlessness as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I remember in grade school getting in trouble for getting out of my seat a lot, talking over the teacher, that kind of thing. I’d rush ahead before they finished directions. My mom used to say I was wound too tight.
Have there been times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
No… not really. I mean, I have nights I sleep poorly, but I don’t feel full of energy after. Usually I’m just tired.
Do you often feel excessively worried or on edge, even when there isn’t an immediate reason?
Not really… I mean, I get stressed like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m worried all the time for no reason.
When you have this restlessness, does it feel like an uncomfortable inner urge to keep moving?

Yeah… that’s pretty much it. It’s like there’s a motor going under my skin when I’m supposed to sit still. In meetings or church briefings, I start shifting around, or I’ll stand up, or find some reason to move.
When you get up and move around, does that restless feeling go away?
Yeah… for a little while. If I get up or find some reason to walk around, it takes the edge off. But once I have to sit still again, that motor feeling kind of comes back.
Are you currently taking an antipsychotic medicine?
Uh… I’m not sure what counts as that. I don’t think so, no.
Does this restless feeling show up mostly when you’re stuck doing something boring or that requires you to stay focused for a while?

Yeah… mostly when I’m supposed to sit still for a while. Like staff meetings or church briefings. I start feeling that motor thing under my skin, and then I’m shifting around or looking for a reason to get up.
Does this same hard-to-sit-still feeling happen in other situations too, not just meetings or church?

Yeah… it can. It’s not only those, but it’s mostly when I’m expected to sit still. I get that kind of motor humming feeling, and I start shifting around or looking for some reason to stand up or move.
Are you taking any medicine for mood, thoughts, or nausea?
Not that I know of. I’m not really on anything like that… at least I don’t think so.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I haven’t really paid close attention to it. Conversations, I can usually manage, I think. Tasks depend, I guess.
Do you often have trouble paying attention when you’re doing work or reading?
I’m not really sure. Reading’s not something I do a whole lot of, and at work I mostly just try to get through what’s in front of me. I haven’t noticed it as a big thing, I guess.
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details at work?
I’m not sure. I mean, little things happen sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than anybody else. No one’s really made a big issue of it with me.
When you feel this restlessness, do you find yourself pacing or repeatedly moving your legs or feet?

Yeah… I do. If I’m supposed to sit still, like in a meeting or something, I’ll be moving my feet or shifting around. Sometimes I’ll just stand up or find a reason to go do something. Feels like there’s a motor running in me, kind of.
Are you taking a stimulant medicine, like Adderall, Vyvanse, or Ritalin?
No… not that I know of. I’m not taking anything like that.
Do you often interrupt people or have trouble waiting your turn?

Yeah… waiting my turn is hard sometimes. Like at work, if I’m waiting on the freight elevator or for the supply closet key, I get pretty antsy. I’ll pace, or I might kind of push to get things moving before it’s really my turn.
When you’re doing something active or interesting, does that restless feeling usually ease up?

Yeah… usually if I’m up doing something, it’s not as bad. It’s more when I’m supposed to sit still—like meetings or church briefings. Then I feel that motor kind of humming, and I end up shifting around or finding a reason to get up.
